title: global-rate-fallback-priority-shedding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: During transient spikes and limiter backend outages we've observed full-per-tenant throttles and unfair token distribution across regions, causing critical customers to experience elevated error rates and missed SLOs. Goal: Implement a global fallback limiter and deterministic priority shedder that preserves SLOs for high-priority tenants, ensures fairness across active regions, and provides fast, observable recovery when the primary quota store degrades. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and runbook updates for the fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: 1) On primary quota-store outage, requests are routed to a local edge fallback limiter with configurable per-tenant emergency credits. 2) High-priority tenants maintain >=99% success under small-medium bursts while lower-priority tenants receive degraded but bounded service. 3) Cross-region reconciliation converges within 60s once quota-store is healthy. 4) There are unit and chaos tests that simulate Redis/consensus failures and verify no unbounded per-tenant token accumulation. 5) Dashboards and alerts for fallback activation, reconciliation lag, and per-tenant throttling are in place.
design_notes:
- Fallback model: local leaky-bucket per region with deterministic deficit-round-robin (DRR) across tenant classes.
- Emergency credits: small per-tenant reserve funded from historical usage pattern or entitlement tier.
- Circuit breaker interplay: limiter enters 'degraded' circuit when quota-store p95 latency > 500ms or error rate > 1%; breaker disables optimistic global windows and switches to conservative local accounting.
- Reconciliation: periodic reconcile where regions exchange compact 'delta ledgers' and resolve via last-write-wins with monotonic counters to avoid negative quotas.
- Fairness: DRR combined with tenant-class weights avoids starvation when a single tenant spikes.
- Metrics: fallback_active{region,tenant_class}, reconcile_lag_seconds, per_tenant_throttle_rate, emergency_credit_consumed, limiter_circuit_state.
- Rollout: staged region-by-region with canary and traffic shadowing; emergency mode can be toggled via console and API for ops.
implementation_steps: 1) Add local leaky-bucket limiter module with DRR output (ENG-9154-a). 2) Implement emergency credit ledger and per-tenant snapshot API (ENG-9154-b). 3) Add circuit-breaker hooks into quota client and limiter (ENG-9154-c). 4) Cross-region delta ledger endpoints and reconciliation worker (ENG-9154-d). 5) Integrate telemetry and dashboards (ENG-9154-e). 6) End-to-end chaos tests and synthetic-burst scenarios (ENG-9154-f). 7) Update runbook and on-call playbook (ENG-9154-g).
tests:
- Unit tests for DRR fairness under mixed-weight tenants.
- Integration test simulating Redis outage and verifying fallback triggers within 2s.
- Chaos test: kill quota-store leader, verify emergency credits keep P0 tenants healthy, and reconcile restores global counters without double-spend.
- Load test: synthetic 200% burst across 3 regions, verify per-tenant throttle rate stays within SLAs.
- Regression test for negative-balance bug discovered during spike postmortem.
updates: 2026-02-10 - Created ticket. Initial problem statement and goals (Ava).
2026-02-12 - Spike: implemented prototype DRR limiter in sandbox; observed fairer allocation vs simple token-bucket (Rohit). Profiling notes attached.

2026-02-15 - Design review with SRE and Product. Decided on small emergency credit pool rather than full optimistic window to avoid double-spend. Action: add reconciliation deltas with monotonic counters (Ava, Rohit).

2026-02-18 - Integration test failing intermittently: reconciliation worker occasionally applied deltas out-of-order. Root cause: clock skew and non-monotonic snapshot IDs. Plan: attach logical vector timestamps to deltas and retry idempotently. (Rohit)
2026-02-20 - PR opened for local limiter and circuit hooks: runtime PR #1429. Draft dashboards pushed to Grafana (link above).

2026-02-24 - Canary deployed to eu-west-1 with traffic shadowing for 1% of requests. Observability: fallback_active fired twice for a 10s Redis GC; emergency credits held P0 tenants above 99.5% success. Continue to monitor reconciliation tidy-up errors.
notes:
- Avoid global locks or synchronous remote calls in the fast path; fallback must be local and bounded.
- Consider future work: adaptive emergency-credit sizing using per-tenant ML predictor (separate ticket).
- Ensure compliance with Private deployments: fallback must not leak cross-tenant data and ledger exchanges should be disabled in air-gapped installs.
